# What is Generative Modelling?

## Classification: $f(\vect{x}) = \vect{y}$

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}basics_classifier.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
**Many-to-one**: many elephant images → one label.
:::


## Generation: $g(\vect{y}) = \vect{x}$

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}basics_elephant.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
**One-to-many**: one label → many possible elephant images.
:::


## Quiz: The Problem {.center}

::: {.r-fit-text}
If the input is just the label "elephant", how can the model generate **different** elephants?
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Answer:** Neural networks are deterministic. We need **stochasticity**.
:::


## Need a Stochastic Function

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}basics_elephants_probabilistic.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
One condition should produce a diverse set of outputs.
:::


## Solution: Latent Variables

::: {.fragment}
Add stochastic input $\vect{z} \sim p(\vect{z})$:

$$\hat{\vect{x}} = g_{\theta}(\vect{y}, \vect{z}), \qquad \vect{z} \sim \mathcal{N}(\mathbf{0}, \mathbf{I})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Latent variable** $\vect{z}$ — unobserved factors:

- pose, size, number of individuals
- time of day, surroundings, lighting
:::

::: {.fragment}
- $\vect{y}$ → **what** to generate (control)
- $\vect{z}$ → **how it varies** (diversity)
:::


## Quiz: Latent Variables {.center}

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}latent_variables_intuition1.png){width=45%}

::: {.fragment}
What could the latent variables be for this dataset?
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Answer:** Width and height — 2 unobserved latent variables.
:::


## Latent Space → Outputs

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}latent_variables_intuition2.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Plausible 2D latent space and the mapping to samples (@foster_generative_2023).
:::


# Unconditional vs. Conditional Generation

## Unconditional Generation

::: {.fragment}
The model receives only stochastic input:

$$\vect{z} \sim p(\vect{z}), \quad \hat{\vect{x}} = g_{\theta}(\vect{z})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
- $\vect{z}$ provides diversity
- different $\vect{z}$ → different plausible outputs
- e.g. "any face", "any room", "any product"
:::


## Conditional Generation

::: {.fragment}
The model also receives conditioning information $\vect{c}$:

$$\hat{\vect{x}} = g_{\theta}(\vect{z}, \vect{c})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
$\vect{c}$ specifies what should be generated, preserved, completed, enhanced, or changed.
:::

::: {.fragment}
> **Key idea:** $\vect{z}$ provides **diversity**, $\vect{c}$ provides **control**.
:::


## Generative CV Beyond Text-to-Image

| Setting | Condition $\vect{c}$ | Example |
|---|---|---|
| Unconditional | none | random face / room |
| Class-conditional | class label | "an elephant" |
| Text-to-image | text prompt | "red chair in modern room" |
| Image editing | image + instruction | change season, style, lighting |
| Inpainting | image + mask | remove object, fill region |
| Outpainting | image + extended canvas | extend background |
| Super-resolution | low-res image | upscale, denoise |
| Image translation | source image | MRI → CT, sketch → photo |
| Layout control | seg/depth/pose/edges | structural control |
| Reference-based | reference image | preserve identity / product |
| Synthetic data | task spec | rare classes, defects |
| Video | prompt / frames | clips, motion |


## Quiz: What Is the Condition? {.center}

| Task | Condition? |
|---|---|
| super-resolution | ? |
| inpainting | ? |
| MRI → CT | ? |
| text-to-image | ? |
| product image from reference | ? |


## Quiz: What Is the Condition? {.center}

| Task | Condition? |
|---|---|
| super-resolution | low-resolution image |
| inpainting | image + mask |
| MRI → CT | source MRI image |
| text-to-image | text prompt |
| product image from reference | reference product image |


## Creative vs. Faithful

::: {.incremental}
- **Creative**: unconditional, text-to-image — needs diversity, plausibility
- **Faithful**: inpainting, super-res, translation, editing — preserve identity, geometry, layout
- Most real systems need **both**
:::

# Learning Generative Models

## The Objective

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}synthetic_quality/synthetic_quality_evaluation.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Generated $\hat{\vect{x}}$ should have **high probability** under the real data distribution $p_{\text{data}}(\vect{x})$.
:::


## Two Approaches

::: {.fragment}
**1. Direct (Implicit)**

Learn a function that generates samples directly:
$$g(\vect{z}) = \vect{x}$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
**2. Indirect (Density)**

Learn a probability density $p_{\theta}(\vect{x})$, then sample from it.
:::


## Density Models

::: {.fragment}
Learn $p_{\theta}: \vect{x} \to [0, \infty)$ with normalization:

$$\int_{\vect{x}} p_{\theta}(\vect{x})\, d\vect{x} = 1$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
Goal: $p_{\theta} \approx p_{\text{data}}$.
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Maximum likelihood objective:**

$$\underset{\theta}{\arg\max} \frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \log p_{\theta}(\vect{x}^{(i)})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Examples:** VAEs, normalizing flows, autoregressive models.
:::


## Learning a Density Model

::: {layout-ncol=2}

![Initial]({{< meta params.images_path >}}density_model_1d/initial_distribution.png)

![Improved]({{< meta params.images_path >}}density_model_1d/improved_distribution.png)

:::

::: {.fragment}
The model adapts to place high probability where training data lies.
:::


## Density ≠ Generation

::: {.fragment}
A density model evaluates $p_{\theta}(\vect{x})$ — useful for **outlier detection**.
:::

::: {.fragment}
To **generate**, we additionally need a sampling mechanism.
:::


# Desirable Properties

## No Free Lunch {.center}

::: {.r-fit-text}
**No single model achieves all desirable properties simultaneously.**
:::


## 1. Efficient Sampling

::: {.incremental}
- Generate new samples quickly
- Critical for real-time and large-scale use
- **Excel:** GANs, normalizing flows (single forward pass)
- **Struggle:** autoregressive, diffusion (sequential steps)
:::


## 2. High-Quality Sampling

::: {.incremental}
- Realistic, detailed, indistinguishable from real
- **Excel:** modern GANs, diffusion, large autoregressive models
- Often paid for with compute or training complexity
:::


## 3. Coverage (Diversity)

::: {.incremental}
- Generate the full diversity of training data
- **Failure mode:** mode collapse (GANs) — limited variety
- **Excel:** VAEs (often at the cost of sample quality)
:::


## 4. Well-Behaved Latent Space

::: {.incremental}
- Smooth, meaningful structure
- Similar $\vect{z}$ → similar outputs
- Enables interpolation and controlled generation
- **Excel:** VAEs (explicit training objective)
:::


## 5. Disentangled Latent Space

::: {.incremental}
- Different dimensions → independent factors
- e.g. separate controls for pose, lighting, color
- Enables fine-grained, interpretable control
- Hard without explicit architectural design
:::


## 6. Efficient Likelihood Computation

::: {.incremental}
- Evaluate $p_{\theta}(\vect{x})$ for any sample
- Enables direct optimization, anomaly detection, model comparison
- **Have:** autoregressive, flows, VAEs (approx)
- **Lack:** GANs, many diffusion models
:::


## Quiz: Why No Perfect Model? {.center}

::: {.r-fit-text}
Why can't one generative model achieve all of these properties at once?
:::

::: {.fragment}
**Answer:** Fundamental tradeoffs — fast sampling vs. exact likelihood, quality vs. coverage, etc.
:::


# Evaluating Generative Models

## Why Evaluation Is Hard

::: {.fragment}
Usually no single correct output. Many outputs may be valid for one input.
:::

::: {.fragment}
Better question than *"is it correct?"*:

> Is the generated image **plausible, diverse, useful, and faithful** to the condition?
:::


## Likelihood

::: {.fragment}
$$\frac{1}{N} \sum_{i=1}^{N} \log p_{\theta}(\vect{x}^{(i)})$$
:::

::: {.fragment}
High likelihood → model assigns high probability to real data.
:::

::: {.incremental}
- Not available for GANs (no explicit density)
- High likelihood ≠ perceptually good samples
:::


## Human Evaluation

::: {.incremental}
- Which image looks more realistic?
- Which better matches the prompt?
- Which has fewer artifacts?
- Which would you prefer to use?
:::

::: {.fragment}
Most meaningful for visual quality — but slow, subjective, expensive.
:::


## Distribution-Level Metrics

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}evaluating_genai.png){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
**Inception Score (IS)** [@salimans_improved_2016]: classifier-based — confident per-image + diverse across set.
:::


## IS / FID / KID — Limitations

::: {.incremental}
- Depend on a pretrained classifier
- Most meaningful for class-balanced data (e.g. ImageNet)
- Don't compare generated images directly to real images
- Don't evaluate prompt adherence or input fidelity
- Can hide failures on rare classes, spatial relations, text rendering
:::


## Conditional Generation Metrics

| Task | What to evaluate? |
|---|---|
| text-to-image | does it match the prompt? |
| image editing | was the change made? |
| inpainting | filled region plausible + consistent? |
| super-resolution | realistic + faithful to input? |
| image translation | target domain reached, content preserved? |
| synthetic data | does it improve downstream performance? |

::: {.fragment}
Prompt alignment often measured with CLIP-based scores.
:::


## Conditional Evaluation in Practice

![]({{< meta params.images_path >}}wine_comparison.jpg){.r-stretch}

::: {.fragment}
Same prompt across different models — judged on realism *and* prompt alignment.
:::


## Task-Specific Evaluation

| Application | Possible evaluation |
|---|---|
| medical translation | anatomical plausibility, expert review, downstream diagnosis |
| synthetic training data | improvement on real validation/test data |
| product image generation | preservation of product identity & geometry |
| super-resolution | perceptual quality, fidelity, downstream task |
| inpainting | boundary consistency, semantic plausibility |

::: {.fragment}
A generated image can look realistic but be scientifically wrong.
:::


## Summary: No Single Metric

| Aspect | Example method |
|---|---|
| realism / fidelity | human judgement, FID, KID |
| diversity / coverage | distribution metrics, class coverage |
| likelihood | test-set log-likelihood (if available) |
| prompt adherence | CLIP-based scores, human judgement |
| input fidelity | reconstruction / preservation metrics |
| downstream utility | model trained on synthetic data |

::: {.fragment}
The right evaluation **depends on the task.**
:::
